summary: At 973ed4c, the synthetic recipe's visible soldier changes into a red dragon at step 70. C mon.c newcham() then runs worn.c mon_break_armor(), which emits and dismisses the suit, shield, helmet, and boots messages across steps 70-74. JavaScript leaves this call as note_unported(), causing five screen mismatches and four cursor mismatches while all 2779 RNG calls still match. Port the complete worn.c m_lose_armor()/mon_break_armor() family and wire it into the existing newcham callers.

source.branch: After mon.c newcham() changes the visible soldier to PM_RED_DRAGON, worn.c mon_break_armor() takes the breakarm() branch. It consumes ordinary body armor after a cracking message, drops the shield and helmet with their messages, drops the boots with the pushed-off-feet message, and preserves the full saddle/riding tail for other forms. m_lose_armor() must extract the worn item, place it at the monster square, set bypass for wand polymorph, and redraw the square in C order.
callers: C mon.c newcham() lines 5484-5488 calls mon_break_armor(mtmp, polyspot) after the shape-change message; js/mon.js apply_newcham_steps() lines 2926-2934 currently records note_unported('worn.c mon_break_armor').
C were.c new_were() lines 95-138 calls mon_break_armor(mon, FALSE) after a successful were_change(); the JS were-change path in js/mon.js reaches the same missing worn.c operation.
The synthetic production caller is the wizard #zap polymorph path: js/zap.js zap_monster() selects the target and awaits js/mon.js newcham_distress(), which owns the same mon.c newcham call boundary.
dependencies: worn.c which_armor() lines 1006-1035 is already implemented in js/worn.js and supplies each worn slot from the monster minvent chain.
worn.c extract_from_minvent() lines 1375-1417 and mthrowu.c m_useup() lines 1153-1170 remove or consume armor; preserve their existing object-mask, extrinsic, weapon, quantity, and free ordering.

mondata.c breakarm(), sliparm(), nohands(), verysmall(), slithy(), has_horns(), and the object predicates Is_dragon_scales(), Is_dragon_mail(), WrappingAllowed(), and is_flimsy() determine each source branch.

steed.c can_saddle()/can_ride()/dismount_steed() and trap.c instapetrify() remain their own source owners for the saddle and dismount tail; preserve discarded-call gaps when those branches are not implemented.
Use the canonical worn-object message and display owners (pline_mon/You_hear, Monnam/s_suffix, surface, newsym) and retain polyspot bypass behavior without adding RNG.

evidence: Queue provenance is the v1 challenge evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260918192720-v1.json at evaluation commit 2ab3d33c4affb45693cc1cdc56882430c63db58f; the immutable recording is challenges/cases/monster-transformations.session.json with SHA-256 5c7ff94dc1e63dcae559231dbea1843d5206c45d8fdb894d107beed35bff5f6b. At examined commit 973ed4c, 76/81 screens and 77/81 cursors match, 2779/2779 RNG calls match, and exactly 5 screens remain.

The saved scan .cache/synthetic-scans/v1/monster-transformations.json identifies the first mismatch at step 70 on the newline after the red-dragon query: C row 0 column 36 is the first '-' of '--More--', JavaScript has a gray space, and C cursor [44,0,1] is still on the message while JavaScript is at [40,19,1]. serializeBug is false.

The C recording's steps 70-74 are the source-ordered armor sequence: 'The soldier turns into a red dragon!--More--'; 'The red dragon breaks out of its armor!--More--'; 'The red dragon can no longer hold its shield!--More--'; 'The red dragon's helmet falls to the floor!--More--'; and 'The red dragon's boots are pushed off its feet!  The red dragon roars!'. The diagnostic is retained at .cache/investigate-synthetic-v1-monster-transformations/diagnostic.json.

C mon.c newcham() lines 5460-5475 emits the transformation line and lines 5484-5488 immediately call possibly_unwield(), worn.c mon_break_armor(), and trap.c mselftouch(). C worn.c mon_break_armor() lines 1177-1335 contains every armor, shield, helmet, boots, saddle, and riding branch. JavaScript's explicit note_unported at js/mon.js:2929 skips the entire function; the separate trap.c mselftouch gap is not the cause because this red dragon has no petrifying touch output.

The actionable scope is a file-port of worn.c m_lose_armor() lines 1038-1051 plus mon_break_armor() lines 1176-1335, with existing helpers wired at their source call sites. The observed branch has no new RNG; the exact RNG parity confirms the defect is the omitted state/output sequence rather than random-state drift.
